summary: Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Toyo University (graduated 1892), Sera Monastery, and with teachers including Enryo Inoue and Sarat Chandra Das. He served as rector of Gohyaku Rakan-ji (~1888–1891) and professor at Toyo University (1916).

Ekyo Uno is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Uno held posts as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji-ha Shōgakuin (attested 1998).
Elaine Fisher specializes in Indology and religious studies. She was a doctoral student at Columbia University (attested 2010) and is attested as a faculty member at Stanford University in 2026.

Eleanor Nesbitt (born 1951) works in religious studies and Indology. She studied at Girton College and the University of Oxford before serving as a professor in Education Studies at the University of Warwick (~1989–2011).

Eleanor Rosch (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at Harvard University under Roger Brown in ~1963–1969. After positions at Connecticut College and Brown University, she became a professor of cognitive psychology at UC Berkeley in 1971.

Elena Bashir specializes in linguistics and Indology. She studied at the University of Michigan (~1980–1988) and later held positions at the University of Chicago, serving as Senior Lecturer Emerita around 2005.

Elena De Rossi Filibeck specializes in Tibetology. She studied East Asian history under Luciano Petech at Sapienza University of Rome (~1966–1971), where she later became an associate professor in 1980.
Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who completed her PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey (attested 1998).

Elena Mucciarelli specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Tübingen, where she held a post from 2016 to 2017, and became Assistant Professor for Hinduism in the Sanskrit Tradition at the University of Groningen in 2020.

Eli Franco (born 1953) works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Charles Malamoud at EPHE and Paris Nanterre, habilitating at the University of Hamburg. He held the chair of Indology at the University of Leipzig from 2004 to 2021.

Elijah Ary (born 1972) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University, where he earned his PhD under Janet Gyatso and Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp.

Eliot Deutsch (1931–2020) was a philosopher and Indologist. He earned his PhD from Columbia University in 1960. He chaired philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and served as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi from 1967 to 2006.

Elisa Freschi (born 1977) specializes in Indology and philosophy. She completed her doctorate under Raffaele Torella, held posts at Sapienza University of Rome and the University of Vienna (~2012–2019), and became Associate Professor at the University of Toronto in ~2020.
Elisa Ganser is an Indologist who is attested in 2026 as a Lektorin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities and as a visiting researcher at the University of Zurich.

Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza (born 1938) is a religious studies scholar educated at Würzburg and Münster. She held professorships at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard Divinity School as Krister Stendahl Research Professor (from 1988).

Elizabeth A. Cecil (born 1981) works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Brown University under James L. Fitzgerald. She taught at Leiden University (~2016–2018) before becoming Assistant Professor of Religion at Florida State University (~2018).

Elizabeth De Michelis specializes in religious studies and Indology. She completed a master's at SOAS and a PhD at the University of Cambridge (~1997–2001), where she became a director in 2000, later joining the University of Oxford's theology faculty.
Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied under Harunaga Isaacson and completed her PhD at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson by 1999.

Elizabeth Errington (born 1951) works in history/archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar and became curator of pre-Islamic South and Central Asian coins at the British Museum in 1993.

Elizabeth Guthrie (born 1955) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Canterbury (~1998) and served as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago (~2004).
